text: The treatment policy edition travels as one workbook file that rwb-access passes unchanged to P3 rwb-case POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads with the table code product_policy and the valid-from date, so every band, floor and range stays with its owner and this service reads out of the file only the presence of its three parts and their row counts. The three parts are one sheet each for the bands, the floors and the ranges, each with a header row; the sheet names, the header rows, the accepted media types and the upload size cap are fixed at contract review with the owner. The state of a load is read through the owner's load read GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}, declared as consumed although the TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A does not list it, and the screen that carries the edition is served through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 because no source names it. The reference-load contract is called through its contract and its fake and is not added to the metadata dependency rows.
why: The parameters and reference data, the reference-load operations and the treatment entity belong to other services under the R-PREC default ruling and the ownership map, and no source gives the table code, the sheet names or a load read, so the transport and the parts have to be fixed as a default before the build; leaving them open would stop the story and inviting the values into rwb-access would create a second copy of a versioned table.

text: The product head proposes the edition and does not submit it. TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives RW-PRODHEAD R only in Rules and parameters, RW-COE CRUD there and RW-RISK RA there, and the legacy permission table gives the C letter to RW-COE and the A letter to RW-RISK. R-PREC puts the Technical Specifications above the story master, and the FSD makes the product head the primary role of the feature, so the story reads the three sources together as: the product head opens the screen, prepares the edition and proposes it with R; a holder of the C letter, RW-COE, submits it through POST /admin/product-policies; and the A letter approves a load on the console reference-load path, which is RWB-P4-AD010-APP's and not this story's. A product head posting an edition is therefore refused 403 with MSG-P4-002, which is the refusal AC3 tests.
why: Three sources disagree on who may act: the FSD calls the product head primary, the TSD gives it R only, and the legacy table gives the C letter to RW-COE; a story that silently granted the product head the C letter would contradict the matrix and a story that removed the product head from the feature would contradict the FSD, so the reading has to be recorded before the build.

text: An accepted edition appends exactly one entry to the local decision-record chain of DP-03 carrying the editionId, the productGroup, the policyVersion label, the loadId the owner answered, the validFrom date, the version in force read from the parameters contract at the time and the caller reference, and nothing else: no band, no floor, no range, no amount, no percentage and no personal field. The record code that marks the entry as a treatment policy edition is not in any source, so the entry uses the DP-03 library's administrative-change code and the contract review fixes the value with the ledger owner. The entry, the idempotency row and the answer commit in one local transaction, and where the entry cannot be written the answer is withheld with 503 and MSG-P7-003, which is what legacy AC2 asserts as nothing changing.
why: Legacy AC1 requires the result to be written to the decision log with the rule version, and legacy AC2 requires nothing to change when the log cannot be written, but no source names the record code of an administrative change or says which version label the entry carries; the record has to be fixed as a default or neither criterion can be tested.
